recent_posts.title: How to set up CodeRabbit for AI code review on your GitHub projects
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on walkthrough of CodeRabbit, an AI-powered code review platform that integrates with GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket. The demo covers setting up CodeRabbit on a Next.js project, understanding its comment categories (critical, major, minor, nitpick), using the GitHub PR workflow to review and address AI-generated code, and using the CodeRabbit CLI and Claude Code plugin to review changes locally before pushing. Key features highlighted include codebase-aware reviews, Linear/CircleCI integrations, MCP server support, configurable review profiles (chill vs assertive), and an organizational knowledge base that learns team conventions over time.

recent_posts.title: 10 email deliverability tips every developer should know
recent_posts.summary: A developer-focused conversation with a DX engineer from Resend covering 10 practical tips for improving email deliverability. General tips include: using subdomains instead of apex domains to isolate sending reputation, warming up domains gradually and predictably, sending only to engaged users, using topic-based segmentation for granular opt-in control, and keeping email size under 102KB. Developer-specific tips cover: respecting API rate limits, setting up webhooks for real-time observability, using Resend's test email suite (e.g. bounced@resend.dev) instead of fake addresses that cause real bounces, preventing unwanted email threading with custom headers, and implementing idempotency keys to avoid duplicate sends during retry logic. The session also includes a live walkthrough of the Resend dashboard covering domains, warm-up calculators, audiences, segments, and topics.

recent_posts.title: Clerk Core 3 released with 50K free users and unlimited apps per plan
recent_posts.summary: Clerk has released two major updates: Clerk Core 3 and a revised pricing plan. Core 3 brings improved customization APIs for custom auth flows, a new theme editor with interactive docs for built-in components, and support for modern React features like transitions, suspense, and streaming, including Next.js 16 cache component support. The pricing update raises the free tier limit from 10,000 to 50,000 retained users and introduces unlimited applications on every paid plan, meaning developers no longer pay per app. Most authentication add-ons are now bundled into the pro plan, with only billing, B2B, and administrative features remaining as add-ons. Automated migration to the new pricing is scheduled for April.

recent_posts.title: Clerk Core 3 + New Pricing: 50K Free Users, Unlimited Apps, and Breaking Changes
recent_posts.summary: Clerk has released two major updates: Core 3 and a new pricing structure. Core 3 brings breaking changes including improved customization APIs with better hooks and state handling, a new interactive theme editor for built-in components, keyless mode support for TanStack Start and React Router, modern React features (concurrent rendering, transitions, suspense), a unified Show component replacing SignedIn/SignedOut/Protect components, and Next.js 16 cache component support. On pricing, the free tier now includes 50,000 monthly active users (up from 10K), and all plans now support unlimited applications — meaning one Pro upgrade covers all your apps. Add-ons have been reorganized into B2B, Billing, and Administration tiers. An automated migration to the new pricing will occur in April, so manual migration beforehand is recommended.

recent_posts.title: How a senior engineer at Clerk actually uses AI to code
recent_posts.summary: A senior engineer at Clerk walks through his real-world AI coding workflow, covering how he evolved from skepticism about GitHub Copilot to daily reliance on Cursor and Claude Opus 4.5. Key practices include starting with tightly scoped prompts and gradually increasing AI responsibility, providing rich context via architecture.md and agents.md files, always writing automated tests to validate AI output, using plan mode for complex tasks, and leveraging AI code review tools like CodeRabbit. A live demo builds a Go/Postgres cat cafe management API end-to-end, illustrating how database schema design remains a human-driven foundation while API boilerplate is delegated to AI. The conversation also covers model selection (preferring Opus 4.5 over 4.6 based on hallucination experience), using PRD files as planning artifacts, and the accelerating pace of change in AI tooling.

recent_posts.title: TanStack Start: Server Components Without the Mental Gymnastics
recent_posts.summary: A deep-dive conversation with Tanner Lindsey, creator of TanStack, covering TanStack Start's architecture as a meta-framework built on TanStack Router. Topics include file-based routing conventions (flat files, directories, dot notation, customizable tokens), isomorphic loaders vs. server functions, how server functions differ from React Server Components, and a preview of TanStack's upcoming composite component API that inverts control from server to client for granular caching and slot-based composition.

recent_posts.title: Setting up AI coding agents to write correct Next.js 16 code using MCP and agents.mmd
recent_posts.summary: A practical walkthrough on configuring AI coding agents to generate correct Next.js 16 code, covering four key mechanisms: MCP servers (including the official Next.js dev tools MCP), Claude's 'skills' feature for reusable agent instructions, the agents.mmd file as a persistent system prompt, and progressive disclosure patterns for context management. Vercel's own evaluation data is cited showing that skills alone without explicit invocation instructions don't improve pass rates, while an agents.mmd approach with a locally downloaded, version-matched Next.js documentation index achieved better results. The recommended pattern keeps agents.mmd concise, references sub-markdown files for specific topics, and instructs the agent to prefer retrieval over pre-training data for Next.js tasks.

recent_posts.title: URL state management in Next.js with nuqs creator François Best
recent_posts.summary: A deep-dive interview and live coding session with François Best, creator of nuqs, covering URL state management in Next.js. The session walks through nuqs fundamentals—replacing useState with useQueryState, using parsers for type safety, and the nuqs/nuqs-server import distinction for React Server Components. Advanced patterns include creating a shared search params descriptor object to derive type-safe loaders, hooks, and link generators; controlling shallow vs. deep (server-triggering) updates; debounce and throttle options for rate-limiting URL updates ('time safety'); and integrating React's useTransition for optimistic UI feedback. The creator also discusses Next.js App Router specifics like async search params, cache component boundaries, and the donut pattern for mixing server and client components.

recent_posts.title: Building open source libraries that led to a vercel acquisition
recent_posts.summary: Hayden Blaylock, DX engineer at Vercel, shares his journey building open source libraries like Kibbo UI (a Shadcn registry for complex components), Next Forge (a Turbo Repo template acquired by Vercel), and Ultrasite (a strict linter/formatter preset). He discusses his philosophy of providing free, composable tools while exploring monetization through hosted services. Now at Vercel, he maintains AI Elements and Streamdown, helping developers build AI interfaces. The conversation covers his transition from frustration-driven development to working on AI SDK tooling, his thoughts on skills vs MCP, and how AI agents are changing software development while fundamentals still matter.
